Printed Southwest Arts and Crafts card lists Indian Pueblos of New Mexico, approximate distances from Santa Fe and dates of annual fiestas, with a notice to dealers below.

Written text (transcribed as written):
Printed card: “INDIAN PUEBLOS OF NEW MEXICO APPROXIMATE DISTANCES FROM SANTA FE AND DATES OF ANNUAL FIESTAS Acoma—150 miles west—Sept. 2 Cochiti—30 miles west—July 14 Isleta—78 miles s. w.—Aug. 28 Jemez—65 miles west—Nov. 12 Laguna—120 miles s. w.—Sept. 19 Picuris—70 miles n. e.—Oct. 4 Nambe—20 miles north—Aug. 10 Sandia—50 miles s. w.—June 13 San Felipe—40 miles s. w.—May 1 San Ildefonso—23 miles n. w.—Jan. 23 San Juan—25 miles north—June 24 Santa Ana—55 miles s. w.—July 26 Santa Clara—30 miles north—Aug. 12 Santo Domingo—30 miles south—Aug. 4 Taos—70 miles n. e.—Sept. 30 Tesuque—10 miles north—Nov. 12 Zia—60 miles s. w.—Aug. 15 Zuni—250 miles west—Early Dec. All information courteously given. We are always glad to have visitors look around. Purchases Packed Free. NOTICE TO DEALERS We are the largest general jobbers of Indian and Mexican handicraft in the Southwest. Wholesale price list on request. Chimayo and Navajo Blankets and Rugs, Table Scarfs, Pil- low Tops, Indian Baskets, Pottery, Jewelry and Beadwork. SOUTHWEST ARTS & CRAFTS JULIUS GANS “At the end of the Santa Fe Trail,” Santa Fe, New Mexico. (Over)”
